summary: Created ITagMergeService in Core/Abstractions: ShowAsync(Tag sourceTag, CancellationToken) returns Task.

Created TagMergeViewModel: SourceTag (read-only), SelectedTargetTag observable (change triggers LoadImpactAsync with CTS cancellation), Impact (TagMergeImpact? shows counts), IsBusy. ExecuteCommand CanExecute: !IsBusy && SelectedTargetTag != null && Impact != null. ExecuteAsync calls MergeTagAsync(SourceTag.TagId, SelectedTargetTag.TagId) then raises CloseRequested. CancelCommand raises CloseRequested. AvailableTags = all tags except source, sorted by NameWithPath.

Created TagMergeView.axaml: source tag TextBlock, target ComboBox, Impact preview panel (IsVisible via ObjectConverters.IsNotNull), Merge/Cancel buttons. Compiled bindings with x:DataType=vm:TagMergeViewModel and models:Tag DataTemplates.
Created AvaloniaTagMergeService: wraps TagMergeViewModel in a 460x340 modal Window, subscribes CloseRequested to close window, awaits ShowDialog.

comments.note: TagMergeViewModel.cs: LoadImpactAsync catches bare Exception and silently leaves Impact=null. This hides DB errors from the user. A toast/snackbar or error label would improve diagnosability, but no error-display mechanism is available in this WP's scope.

TagMergeViewModel.cs: _impactLoadCts is never disposed on VM tear-down. In practice the dialog is short-lived, so this is not a resource leak concern, but implementing IDisposable for correctness would be clean.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified and met.
AC1: OnSelectedTargetTagChanged fires LoadImpactAsync which calls GetMergeImpactAsync; sets Impact property; ExecuteCommand only enabled when Impact!=null && SelectedTargetTag!=null && !IsBusy.
AC2: ExecuteAsync calls _tagsManager.MergeTagAsync(SourceTag.TagId, target.TagId) — correct source/target ID ordering verified in source.

AC3: TagsManager.MergeTagAsync (WP-009) calls ReloadAsync then RaiseDataChanged. MoviesListViewModel (WP-010) subscribes to DataChanged and triggers debounced LoadAsync — source tag absent from reloaded list. Code-chain verified.
AC4: ITagMergeService interface declares ShowAsync(Tag sourceTag, CancellationToken=default). AvaloniaTagMergeService passes sourceTag to TagMergeViewModel constructor.
AC5: Build confirmed 0 errors, 0 warnings. Regression: all 685 tests passing.

comments.note: TagMergeViewModel: LoadImpactAsync silently swallows non-cancellation exceptions (catch Exception block leaves Impact=null). A failed DB call is indistinguishable from 'not yet loaded', so ExecuteCommand stays disabled with no user-visible error. Low priority for a dialog VM but could confuse users.

AC3 (source tag no longer visible after merge) is verified by the chain: TagsManager.MergeTagAsync → ReloadAsync → RaiseDataChanged → MoviesListViewModel.OnTagsDataChanged → DebouncedLoadAsync. The 150ms debounce means the list updates 150ms after merge dialog closes. Verified via code-chain analysis across WP-009/010/013.

summary: PASS — WP-013 is clean and compact. TagMergeViewModel handles the impact-preview lifecycle correctly.
OnSelectedTargetTagChanged: CTS cancel/replace pattern is safe here (UI-thread-only partial method), unlike the event handler version in MoviesListViewModel.
LoadImpactAsync: cancellation guard (!cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested) before Impact = impact is a defensive extra check beyond the OperationCanceledException catch. Correct.
ExecuteAsync: IsBusy reset in finally before CloseRequested fires — consistent with the Fix-Forward applied to WP-011's SaveAsync.

comments.note: TagMergeViewModel: No Fix-Forward needed. ExecuteAsync correctly resets IsBusy in finally before firing CloseRequested. LoadImpactAsync guards IsBusy reset with !cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested to avoid resetting on cancelled operations. OnSelectedTargetTagChanged Cancel/Dispose is safe because it always runs on the UI thread (property change callback), unlike MoviesListViewModel.OnTagsDataChanged which fires from an event.
